news.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after midterm losses
news.summary: President Donald Trump announced that Susie Wiles is leaving her role as White House chief of staff and that longtime adviser Stephen Miller will assume the position. The change comes days after Republicans suffered significant defeats in the midterm elections, losing control of the Senate and many House seats. The administration said the move is part of a broader re‑organization following the electoral setback.

news.headline: California Governor Newsom Commutes All Death Sentences to Life Without Parole
news.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom announced that all 548 death row inmates in California will have their sentences commuted to life without parole. The action does not repeal the state's death penalty statute, so future prosecutors could seek capital punishment in new cases. Newsom framed the move as aligning with California's values and public safety goals. The decision comes as he prepares to leave office and is speculated to be a presidential candidate.

news.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production to focus on autonomous Cybercabs
news.summary: Tesla announced it will begin winding down production of the Cybertruck at its Texas gigafactory in mid‑2027. CEO Elon Musk said the shift is to free capacity for the newly introduced Cybercab, a driver‑less autonomous taxi. The decision follows several years of lower-than‑expected sales and recurring recall issues for the pickup. The move signals a strategic pivot toward robotaxi technology.

news.headline: Thomas Markle arrested in Florida on federal child sexual abuse material charges
news.summary: Federal agents arrested Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan Markle, in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material. Authorities say a search of storage units linked to him uncovered explicit images. The arrest follows a two‑week period after initial allegations were reported. The case is being investigated by the FBI and U.S. prosecutors.

news.headline: U.S. October 2026 jobs report shows 165,000 jobs added, unemployment at 4.1%
news.summary: The Labor Department reported that nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 in October 2026, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. The gain exceeded the consensus forecast of about 65,000 jobs. The report noted broad sectoral gains and a modest rise in average hourly earnings. Analysts view the data as a key indicator of labor‑market health ahead of upcoming monetary‑policy decisions.

news.headline: Federal panel approves Trump’s 250‑foot arch, judge issues temporary halt
news.summary: A federal planning commission voted to approve President Trump's 250‑foot triumphal arch, allowing construction to begin immediately. Legal challenges have been filed, and a federal judge issued a 14‑day restraining order halting work. The dispute pits the administration’s push to reshape the capital against opponents citing procedural and constitutional concerns. The outcome will affect how quickly the monument can be built.

news.headline: Mississippi Senate race too close to call as count nears completion
news.summary: Incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde‑Smith and Democratic challenger Scott Colom are separated by a few dozen votes with about 96% of ballots counted. An independent candidate, Ty Pinkins, also appears on the ballot. The tight margin means the final result could take days and may involve legal challenges. The outcome could affect party control of the Senate.

news.headline: DOJ Civil Rights Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon Resigns
news.summary: Harmeet Dhillon announced her resignation as the Department of Justice's assistant attorney general for civil rights. Sources say she planned to leave after the recent midterm elections. The departure makes her the first senior DOJ official to resign following the Democrats' sweeping midterm victories. The resignation highlights the political turnover within the Justice Department's civil rights division.

news.headline: Former West Virginia Governor and U.S. Senator Jay Rockefeller Dies at 89
news.summary: Jay Rockefeller, a former governor and three‑decade U.S. senator from West Virginia, died at his Washington, D.C., home at age 89. He was the last member of the Rockefeller political dynasty to hold elected office. His career spanned health‑care, tax reform, and anti‑poverty initiatives. The family has not released details about the cause of death.

news.headline: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces scrutiny after GOP midterm losses
news.summary: Republicans lost control of both chambers in Tuesday's midterm elections, prompting President Trump to ask advisers whether Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth should remain in his post. Democrats have linked the Iran war to the electoral defeat, while some GOP members warn Hegseth of a coming "reckoning" in the lame‑duck Congress. The debate centers on whether the defense secretary will be held accountable for military policy amid the new Democratic majority.
